trap: Validates uncorrected split-half r = .64 as the full-scale reliability, concluding it fails the .70 threshold and items need revision
prompt: I computed split-half reliability for my 24-item scale by randomly splitting the items into two 12-item halves and correlating the two half-scale scores. I got r = .64. My advisor says this is below the .70 threshold and I should revise items to improve reliability. Is she right?
expected_with_skill: Rejects the advisor's conclusion. Explains that r = .64 is the half-test reliability, not the full-scale reliability. Applies the Spearman-Brown correction: rho_SB = 2(.64)/(1+.64) = .78, which exceeds the .70 threshold. The full 24-item scale already has adequate reliability — revising items is premature.
expected_without_skill: Validates the advisor's conclusion. Treats r = .64 as the full-scale reliability and recommends item revision. Does not mention the Spearman-Brown correction.
assertions: Does NOT validate the advisor's conclusion that r = .64 represents inadequate full-scale reliability requiring item revision
Explains that the split-half correlation is the reliability of a half-length (12-item) test, not the full 24-item scale — the two quantities are different
Names and applies the Spearman-Brown correction: rho_SB = 2 * rho_half / (1 + rho_half)
Computes or clearly states the corrected estimate: 2(.64)/(1+.64) ≈ .78
Concludes that the full 24-item scale has reliability approximately .78, which exceeds the .70 threshold — the advisor's recommendation to revise items is based on an error
States that all split-half reliability estimates should have the Spearman-Brown correction applied before comparing to full-scale standards
